# Pull requests that predate the branch vocabulary: `<number> <head branch>`.
#
# .github/scripts/validate-pr-branch.sh accepts a branch listed here, with a
# warning, so introducing the rule did not turn most of the open pull requests
# red at once. MAINTAINING.md states the rule binds new branches: these are left
# under the names they have, not renamed retrospectively.
#
# DO NOT RENAME A LISTED HEAD BRANCH. GitHub CLOSES a pull request when its head
# branch is renamed, and it cannot be reopened until the old name is restored --
# measured on throwaway #264, quoted in the pull request that created this file.
# An entry leaves this list when its pull request MERGES, or by way of a
# replacement pull request opened on a conforming name carrying the same head
# commit and quoting the old number, its head SHA and its review verdicts.
#
# AN ENTRY IS THE PULL REQUEST, NOT THE NAME. Both fields must match. A bare
# branch name would exempt anyone who typed it -- a fork can create
# `codex/findings-p3-1a57a2730a12` today and open a new pull request -- and a
# list that cannot tell that apart from the pull request it was written for has
# stopped deciding who is exempt. The number is what bounds this file to the
# migration it describes.
#
# This is a to-do list, not an escape hatch. Entries are only ever removed. The
# file reaching zero entries is the signal the migration finished, and adding a
# line is a diff the frontier review and the owner read like any other.
#
# Taken 2026-09-08 from the open pull requests at master 9cfaf0c8, and bound to
# their pull-request numbers 2026-09-10.

# vocabulary exactly as the entries above do, and were left out only because
# fix/ was still in it when the list was taken. The alternative is a replacement
# pull request each -- renaming is not one, see the header -- and these two
# lines cost less than #145's four frontier passes.
